LESSON: SHORT FORMS • I-P

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: English Braille
Topic 4.2: Short Forms • I-P
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Short Forms • I-P, part of English Braille in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why are short forms important in Braille reading and writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use tactile flashcards to feel and name short form words from I–P, then say a sentence orally using the word,

2. sort Braille cards into short forms and full words (e.g., “people” vs. “p”), then explain their sorting choices,

3. construct short Braille sentences using I–P short forms with slate and stylus, and swap them with classmates for reading and review,

4. play a tactile short form matching game, connecting Braille short form cards to picture cards that represent the full words,

5. race to write five words using short forms from I–P and check who finishes first correctly,

6. explore a Braille paragraph, underlining or marking short forms from I–P, and then read it aloud for fluency,

7. create a tactile Braille short form “word wall” with each learner

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use tactile flashcards to feel and name short form words from I–P, then say a sentence orally using the word,
2. sort Braille cards into short forms and full words (e.g., “people” vs. “p”), then explain their sorting choices,
3. construct short Braille sentences using I–P short forms with slate and stylus, and swap them with classmates for reading and review,
4. play a tactile short form matching game, connecting Braille short form cards to picture cards that represent the full words,
5. race to write five words using short forms from I–P and check who finishes first correctly,
6. explore a Braille paragraph, underlining or marking short forms from I–P, and then read it aloud for fluency,
7. create a tactile Braille short form “word wall” with each learner

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Short Forms • I-P together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner differentiates between short forms and regular words.

● Learning to Learn: the learner practices and reflects on using short forms in writing.

Values:
Responsibility: the learner takes ownership of correctly applying short forms in their writing and strive to use short forms

appropriately to ensure clear communication.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Literacy Development: the learner reinforces Braille literacy skills and improves efficiency in written expression.

● Digital Inclusion: the learner uses assistive digital tools to access and create Braille content independently.

● Peer Learning: the learner collaborates with peers through shared reading and writing tasks to enhance Braille literacy.
